name: Nestlé Cascade Locks Bottling Plant
decision_label: County voters prohibited commercial water bottling
summary: A proposed bottled-water plant was stopped after Hood River County voters adopted a commercial water-bottling prohibition. This cross-sector case provides a longer post-decision window but is not a data-center analogue.
proposal_description: Nestlé sought to develop a bottling operation in Cascade Locks using spring water associated with a proposed water-right exchange. The proposal became a countywide dispute over public water, employment, and local control.

proposed_scale.label: Proposed water use
proposed_scale.value: More than 100 million gallons per year discussed in the proposal

site_afterlife: Parcel-level reuse has not yet been established in this dataset. Current Port of Cascade Locks tenant information documents continuing industrial activity in the community but is not treated as proof of reuse of the exact proposed parcel.
evidence_note: Cross-sector comparison. The longer post-period is useful descriptively, but differences in water use, labor, utilities, and tax treatment prevent a direct one-for-one comparison with a data center.
unresolved_questions: What became of the exact proposed bottling-plant parcel after the vote?
Did any water-right or exchange proceeding survive the county prohibition?
Which contemporaneous fiscal and employment projections can be reconciled to realized county outcomes?

timeline.title: Bottling proposal and water exchange enter public review
timeline.summary: Nestlé's Cascade Locks proposal contemplated a large bottling facility supplied through a spring-water exchange with the city.

timeline.title: Independent preliminary review describes the proposal
timeline.summary: An Oregon State University report summarized a roughly $50 million, 250,000-square-foot facility, possible enterprise-zone benefits, employment claims, and unresolved economic and environmental questions.

timeline.title: County prohibition qualifies for the ballot process
timeline.summary: Local organizers advanced a county charter measure prohibiting commercial water bottling, turning the long-running dispute into a countywide vote.

timeline.title: County voters adopt water-bottling prohibition
timeline.summary: Measure 14-55 passed with roughly two-thirds support and stopped the proposed plant from proceeding on its planned basis.

timeline.title: Retrospective documents the coalition and continuing legal history
timeline.summary: A later case history describes the countywide coalition, the vote, and disputes that continued after the measure passed.

timeline.title: Community-level activity is documented; parcel reuse remains unresolved
timeline.summary: The port lists current industrial tenants, including pFriem operations, but this release does not equate those premises with the exact Nestlé proposal site.

county_outcome_context.note: Hood River County is the only case in this release with a meaningful full-year post-decision window: eight complete years from 2017 through 2024. The county series is descriptive and cannot isolate the prohibition from tourism, migration, the pandemic, or unrelated business activity.
